title: Checksum reconciliation and canary boot validation for Private/VPC upgrades
creator: Imani Duarte
description: PRD: This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for a checksum-based artifact reconciliation and canary boot validation workflow used during Private/VPC upgrades (including air‑gapped and intermittent‑egress sites). Goal: enable operators to perform staged upgrades that are resilient to flaky network egress and that guarantee artifact integrity without relying on live cloud verifications. Non-goals: building a new artifact distribution mirror; replacing existing signed image verification (we integrate with it). Context: Customers in regulated environments often restrict egress and permit short maintenance windows. We need an orchestrated flow that: 1) passes cryptographic verification when egress is unavailable, 2) allows small delta-only downloads during surgical egress windows, and 3) provides deterministic reconciliation when nodes disagree about artifact state. This reduces failed upgrades, operator time, and security exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: When egress is fully blocked, a node can apply an offline delta bundle and validate it using an on-disk manifest signed by Redwood’s release key; the node must reject the bundle if checksum or signature mismatches.

During a permitted egress window, nodes must be able to fetch a delta index (<= 10MB) and validate SHA256 checksums for each file; failure modes must not leave nodes in a partially-applied state (transactional apply or automatic rollback).

Canary cohort (configurable, default 3 nodes) must complete upgrade and boot into healthy state within 30 minutes for 95% of canary runs across simulated network jitter; failure in >5% of runs triggers automatic halt of rollout and operator notification.

Checksum reconciliation: if two or more nodes in the same site disagree on final artifact manifest after upgrade, a deterministic merge protocol must mark nodes as inconsistent, create a reconciliation job, and surface mismatched file paths and SHA256 values in the Console.
All bundles and manifests must be encrypted-at-rest and signed; Console and operator CLI must surface the signing key ID and signature verification result for every applied bundle.

Operator-driven manual apply: operator can mark a specific bundle as approved for a single-node override only after acknowledging risk; the action must be logged with user, timestamp, reason, and must require a secondary approver in high-security sites.
End-to-end test vectors (see test_plan) must pass in an isolated lab with simulated intermittent egress (0s, 30s, 5m windows).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Implement manifest format and bundle signer integration in runtime (feature flag off).
Phase 1: Add canary boot probe and transactional apply code; run internal canaries on staging fleet for 3 weeks.
Phase 2: Beta release to 2 pilot customers with manual operator guidance and runbook; collect failures and adjust timeouts.
Phase 3: Gradual enable by default for Private deployments with Dashboard indicators and automatic halt on canary failures.
test_plan: Synthetic canary tests: run 50 canary upgrades under 3 network profiles (stable, jitter, short-ejection) and assert success rate >= 95% within 30 minutes.
Offline bundle validation tests: corrupt a single byte in an offline bundle and assert nodes refuse to apply and surface a clear error code.
Reconciliation tests: induce divergent manifests on 3 nodes and assert the reconciliation job detects mismatches and provides repair suggestions.
Operator override tests: verify manual override path requires secondary approver and records audit log entries; ensure override still verifies checksum and signature before allow-listing.
monitoring_and_alerting: Console: add ‘Upgrade Cohort Health’ panel showing canary success rate, median apply time, and top failure reasons.
Alert: P1 alert if canary failure rate > 5% in any rollout for > 15 minutes.
Audit trail: every bundle apply must emit an event with fields [bundle_id, manifest_sha256, node_id, operator, signature_ok].
Reconciliation jobs that exceed expected repair time (default 10m) escalate to on-call infra with playbook link.
rollback_and_operator_runbook: If canary fails: automatic halt, create rollback job on canary nodes to last-known-good manifest and notify operator.
For partial-apply detection: runtime must attempt a transactional rollback; if rollback fails, mark node as quarantined and provide recovery steps (reinstall from offline artifact or manual reimage).
Operator runbook steps included: pre-upgrade checklist, how to start ephemeral egress window, verification checklist, and manual reconciliation commands (CLI snippets) with expected outputs.
Runbook must include ‘egress-less recovery’ option that details how to reconstruct a node using only on-site media and signed manifests.
